title: Shared Weights, Selected Computations: How Looped Transformers Route What Each Loop Does
abstract: arXiv:2609.39892v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Looped Transformers repeatedly apply the same set of Transformer layers, giving them a recurrent architecture for latent computation. Their strong performance on iterative reasoning and length-generalization tasks suggests an appealing explanation: recurrence may provide an inductive bias that lets the model reuse a learned algorithm across loops. However, weight sharing alone does not imply that every loop performs the same operation. This raises a basic question: is each loop actually repeating the same computation, and if not, what routes the shared parameters to different operations?   We study this question using graph walks as a test case. In the model's native trajectories, decoded predictions can advance by different numbers of graph steps or remain at a reached target, showing that recurrent progress need not follow a fixed one-loop-one-step pattern. translated_title: 共享权重、选择计算：循环Transformer如何路由每次循环所执行的操作
translated_abstract: 循环Transformer重复应用同一组Transformer层，从而形成一种用于潜在计算的循环架构。它们在迭代推理和长度泛化任务上的出色表现暗示了一个颇具吸引力的解释：循环性可能提供一种归纳偏置，使模型能够跨循环复用已学习的算法。然而，仅凭权重共享并不能保证每次循环都执行相同的操作。这就引出了一个基本问题：每次循环是否真的在重复相同的计算？如果不是，又是什么机制将共享参数路由到不同的操作上？我们以图上的游走作为测试用例来研究这一问题。在模型的原生轨迹中，解码出的预测可以一次推进不同数量的图步数，或停留在已到达的目标节点上，这表明循环式的推进并不必遵循固定的“一次循环走一步”的模式。我们随后展示了一个冻结的循环可以被引导向不同的图上转移……
tldr: 该论文发现循环Transformer中的权重共享并不意味着每次循环执行相同计算——通过图游走实验证明各循环可推进不同的图步数，且冻结的循环还可被引导执行不同的转移操作。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that weight sharing in looped transformers does not guarantee identical computations per loop—graph walk experiments reveal loops can advance varying numbers of graph steps, and a frozen loop can be steered toward different transitions.
